mainTopic: Juice that seeps from fruit on שבת: רבי יהודה's leniency, mulberries and pomegranates, and the challenge from unwilling milk
overview: The משנה teaches that from a barrel that breaks on שבת you may save three meals' worth, but you may not soak up the liquid. It forbids squeezing fruit. The תנא קמא also forbids juice that seeps out by itself, while רבי יהודה permits it when the fruit was meant for eating. It ends with honeycombs crushed before שבת, which the תנא קמא forbids and רבי אליעזר permits. The גמרא adds two ברייתות teaching that on שבת you should not act the way you would on a weekday. It then brings several views on whether רבי יהודה's leniency covers olives and grapes, which are normally squeezed. רבי יוחנן rules like רבי יהודה for other fruits but not for olives and grapes. In רבה's version of שמואל, the two sides agree on both kinds of fruit. רב נחמן בר יצחק therefore places their dispute on mulberries and pomegranates, and a ברייתא confirms it. The גמרא then asks how רבי יהודה can forbid fruit brought in with no stated purpose, quoting a משנה about milk that comes out unwillingly. That quoted debate continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Saving food from a broken barrel
steps.stepSummary: If a barrel of wine or oil breaks on שבת, you may save three meals' worth. You may invite others to save for themselves. But you may not soak it up.
steps.simpleTranslation: A barrel that broke: we may save from it food for three meals. He may also tell others, 'Come and save for yourselves.' This is only allowed as long as he does not soak up the liquid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the rule for a barrel of wine or oil that breaks on שבת. You may rescue a limited amount, and you may not soak up the spill.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The limit of three meals keeps the rescue from becoming a full weekday-style salvage job. Others may each save three meals for themselves. Soaking up liquid with a sponge or cloth is forbidden, because it could lead to squeezing (סחיטה).

keyTerms.meaning: Three meals, the amount needed for שבת
He soaks up, as with a sponge

phrases.english: MISHNA: A barrel that broke
phrases.notes: A barrel of wine or oil, broken on שבת

phrases.english: one may rescue from it food for three meals,
and he may say to others: Come and rescue for yourselves.
Provided that he does not soak it up.
phrases.notes: Soaking it up with a sponge or cloth could end up squeezing it out.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: From a broken barrel you may save three meals' worth, and so may others, but you may not sponge up the liquid.

steps.title: Squeezing fruit and juice that seeps out by itself
steps.stepSummary: You may not squeeze fruit for its juice. The תנא קמא forbids even juice that seeps out by itself. רבי יהודה permits it when the fruit was meant for eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: We may not squeeze fruits to get liquid out of them. If liquid came out on its own, it is forbidden. רבי יהודה says: if the fruit was meant for eating, what comes out is permitted. If it was meant for drinking, what comes out is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה forbids squeezing fruit on שבת. It then records a מחלוקת about juice that drips out on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא forbids the self-seeping juice in every case. This is a safeguard so that a person will not come to squeeze. רבי יהודה says it depends on what the owner had in mind for the fruit. If he wanted the fruit as food, the juice was never something he was after, so there is no worry. If he wanted it for juice, the juice is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: By themselves, without anyone doing anything
Meant for drinking, that is, for juice

steps.confusionAlert: Squeezing itself is forbidden according to everyone. The מחלוקת is only about juice that came out by itself.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין סוֹחֲטִין אֶת הַפֵּירוֹת לְהוֹצִיא מֵהֶן מַשְׁקִין,
phrases.english: One may not squeeze fruits to extract liquids from them,
and if they came out on their own, they are forbidden.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
If the fruits were for eating, what comes out of them is permitted.
And if they were for liquids, what comes out of them is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין סוֹחֲטִין אֶת הַפֵּירוֹת לְהוֹצִיא מֵהֶן מַשְׁקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next ruling in the same משנה, still about liquids on שבת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Squeezing fruit is forbidden. The תנא קמא forbids self-seeping juice, while רבי יהודה permits it if the fruit was meant for eating.

steps.title: Honeycombs crushed before שבת
steps.stepSummary: Honey that drips out on שבת from honeycombs crushed before שבת is forbidden by the תנא קמא. רבי אליעזר permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Honeycombs that were crushed on Friday, and honey came out of them on its own: it is forbidden. רבי אליעזר permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with a case of honeycombs crushed on ערב שבת that keep dripping on שבת. It records a מחלוקת about the honey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the crushing was done before שבת, the תנא קמא treats the honey that drips out on שבת like juice that seeps from fruit, so it is forbidden. רבי אליעזר disagrees and allows it.

phrases.english: Honeycombs that one crushed on Shabbat eve,
and the honey came out on its own: it is forbidden,
and Rabbi Eliezer permits it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the topic of self-seeping liquid to honeycombs
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Honey that seeps on שבת from combs crushed before שבת is forbidden by the תנא קמא and permitted by רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: Do not soak up wine or scoop up oil
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the משנה's 'do not soak up.' You may not sponge up wine or scoop up oil by hand, because that is how you would act on a weekday.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: he should not soak up wine, and he should not scoop up oil with his hand, so that he does not act the way he acts on a weekday.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that adds detail to the broken-barrel rule in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives a second reason beyond squeezing. On שבת a person should not handle a spill the way he would on a regular weekday. That is why collecting oil by patting or cupping it in the hand is also not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Pat or scoop up liquid with the hand
The way he does it on a weekday

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught:
He may not soak up wine
and he may not collect oil with his hand,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יַעֲשֶׂה כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁהוּא עוֹשֶׂה בַּחוֹל.
phrases.english: so that he does not act the way he acts on a weekday.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the משנה's ruling 'provided that he does not soak up'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sponging wine and scooping oil are forbidden because they are weekday behavior.

steps.title: Picking up scattered fruit in a courtyard
steps.stepSummary: If fruit spills in a courtyard on שבת, you may pick it up a little at a time and eat it. You may not gather it into a basket or box, because that is weekday behavior.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: if fruit scattered for someone in a courtyard, he may gather it bit by bit and eat it. But he may not gather it into a basket or into a box, so that he does not act the way he acts on a weekday.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that uses the same principle of 'not like a weekday,' this time for spilled fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picking up a few pieces to eat right away is normal שבת eating. Collecting all of it into a container looks like weekday harvesting or cleanup work, so it is forbidden. This ברייתא shows the 'weekday manner' idea is a general rule, not just a rule about liquids.

keyTerms.meaning: Little by little, one handful at a time

steps.whatToRemember: On שבת, even permitted activities must not be done 'כדרך שהוא עושה בחול', in the way you would do them on a weekday.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
If his fruit was scattered in a courtyard,

phrases.aramaic: מְלַקֵּט עַל יָד עַל יָד, וְאוֹכֵל,
phrases.english: he may gather a little at a time and eat,
but not into the basket
and not into the box,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יַעֲשֶׂה כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁהוּא עוֹשֶׂה בַּחוֹל.
phrases.english: so that he does not act the way he acts on a weekday.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: נִתְפַּזְּרוּ לוֹ פֵּירוֹת בֶּחָצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ברייתא that uses the same principle of avoiding weekday behavior
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scattered fruit may be picked up bit by bit and eaten, but not gathered into a container.

steps.title: רבי יהודה agrees about olives and grapes
steps.stepSummary: Quoting the משנה, רב יהודה says in the name of שמואל that רבי יהודה agrees with the חכמים that juice seeping from olives and grapes is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'We may not squeeze fruits.' רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: רבי יהודה agreed with the חכמים about olives and grapes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the second part of the משנה and limits רבי יהודה's leniency. It does not apply to olives and grapes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to שמואל, רבי יהודה's 'for eating' leniency covers ordinary fruits only. For olives and grapes, juice that seeps out is forbidden even if the owner meant them for eating.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, here the תנא קמא of the משנה

phrases.english: We learned in the mishna: One may not squeeze fruits.
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Rabbi Yehuda concedes to the Rabbis
with regard to olives and grapes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: מוֹדֶה הָיָה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לַחֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens analysis of רבי יהודה's view in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה's leniency does not apply to olives and grapes.

steps.title: Why are olives and grapes different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind שמואל's limit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה would make an exception for olives and grapes. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If what matters is that the owner meant the fruit for eating, why should the kind of fruit make a difference? The גמרא wants the reasoning spelled out.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason olives and grapes are excluded from רבי יהודה's leniency

steps.title: Olives and grapes are made for squeezing
steps.stepSummary: Olives and grapes are normally squeezed, so the owner has their juice in mind even if he set them aside for eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since they are meant for squeezing, he has his mind on them, that is, on their juice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that olives and grapes are normally pressed. So their juice is always on the owner's mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner's plan to eat them does not cancel the usual use of olives and grapes. Since he still thinks of their juice, the juice that drips out is wanted, and it is forbidden just as it is according to the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: He gives his mind to it, he has it in mind

phrases.english: Since they are meant for squeezing,
he has his mind on their juice.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because olives and grapes are normally squeezed, the owner always has their juice in mind.

steps.title: רב says רבי יהודה disagrees even about olives and grapes
steps.stepSummary: עולא in the name of רב disagrees with שמואל. רבי יהודה's leniency applies even to olives and grapes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And עולא said in the name of רב: רבי יהודה disagreed even about olives and grapes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different view. According to רב, רבי יהודה made no exception at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, what decides the case is only what the owner intended for this fruit. If he meant olives or grapes for eating, the juice that seeps out is permitted, just as with other fruits.

phrases.english: And Ulla said that Rav said:
Rabbi Yehuda disagreed
even with regard to olives and grapes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוּלָּא אָמַר רַב: חָלוּק הָיָה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opposes שמואל's limit on רבי יהודה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב, רבי יהודה permits self-seeping juice even from olives and grapes meant for eating.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's halachic ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules like רבי יהודה for other fruits, but not for olives and grapes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה for other fruits, and the הלכה does not follow רבי יהודה for olives and grapes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the practical ruling. He divides between ordinary fruits and olives and grapes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's wording suggests he holds, like רב, that רבי יהודה did disagree about olives and grapes. In practice, though, he rules against רבי יהודה there. So juice from ordinary fruit meant for eating is permitted, and juice from olives and grapes is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the view of...
Other fruits, all fruits besides olives and grapes

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line for juice that drips from fruit on שבת.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda with regard to other fruits,
and the halakha does not follow Rabbi Yehuda
with regard to olives and grapes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בִּשְׁאָר פֵּירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ruling that matches שמואל's practical result
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, juice that seeps from other fruits meant for eating is permitted, and from olives and grapes it is forbidden.

steps.title: רבה's version: each side concedes to the other
steps.stepSummary: רבה quotes שמואל differently. רבי יהודה agrees about olives and grapes, and the חכמים agree with רבי יהודה about other fruits.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said in the name of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל: רבי יהודה agreed with the חכמים about olives and grapes, and the חכמים agree with רבי יהודה about other fruits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another version of שמואל's statement. This version adds that the חכמים also concede something to רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first version said only that רבי יהודה concedes about olives and grapes. רבה's version adds that the חכמים permit juice seeping from other fruits meant for eating. This greatly narrows the מחלוקת, leaving both sides holding almost the same position.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a third אמורא arguing. It is a second report of what שמואל himself said, with an added clause.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה's version of שמואל, everyone forbids juice from olives and grapes, and everyone permits juice from other fruits meant for eating.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabba said that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Rabbi Yehuda would concede to the Rabbis
with regard to olives and grapes,
and the Rabbis would concede to Rabbi Yehuda
with regard to other fruits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fuller version of שמואל's statement from step 6, adding the חכמים's concession
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both sides agree: olives and grapes are forbidden, and other fruits meant for eating are permitted.

steps.title: If they agree on both kinds of fruit, where do they disagree?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks רבי אבא where the real dispute is, and רבי אבא tells him to go look for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to רבי אבא: Then about what do they disagree? He answered: Go look, and you will find it.
steps.whatsHappening: In רבה's version of שמואל, both sides agree, so רבי ירמיה asks where the argument between רבי יהודה and the חכמים actually is. רבי אבא does not give a direct answer. He tells him to search for it, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11, רבי יהודה agrees about זיתים and ענבים, and the חכמים agree about other fruits. That seems to leave nothing to argue about. רבי אבא's reply, 'לכי תשכח', means the dispute exists but has to be found.

keyTerms.meaning: When you look, you will find it (go search)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to Rabbi Abba:
But then, about what do they disagree?
phrases.notes: If both sides agree on olives/grapes and on other fruits, what is left?

phrases.english: He said to him: When you search, you will find it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבה's version of שמואל, which seems to remove the dispute
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In which case do רבי יהודה and the חכמים actually disagree?

steps.title: They disagree about mulberries and pomegranates
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the dispute is about תותים and רמונים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It makes sense that they disagree about mulberries and pomegranates.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives the answer רבי אבא held back. The argument is about mulberries and pomegranates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These fruits are in the middle. They are not always squeezed like olives and grapes, but people do sometimes squeeze them for juice. That in-between status is where רבי יהודה and the חכמים split.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / it is reasonable

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
It is reasonable that they disagree about mulberries and pomegranates.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is about תותים and רמונים, fruits in between olives/grapes and ordinary fruits

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the dispute about mulberries and pomegranates
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says everyone forbids juice from olives and grapes. For mulberries and pomegranates, רבי יהודה permits it only if they were brought in for eating, while the חכמים forbid it in every case.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: If someone squeezed oil from olives or wine from grapes and then brought them in, whether for eating or for juice, what seeps out is forbidden. If someone squeezed juice from mulberries or pomegranates and brought them in for eating, what seeps out is permitted. If he brought them in for juice, or without saying why, it is forbidden. These are the words of רבי יהודה. The חכמים say: whether for eating or for juice, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim. It shows that the dispute is exactly about mulberries and pomegranates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For olives and grapes, both sides forbid the juice, which matches step 11. For mulberries and pomegranates, רבי יהודה lets the owner's plan to eat them decide, but forbids the juice if they were for juice or סתם. The חכמים forbid the juice even when the owner planned to eat them.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה's leniency for mulberries and pomegranates covers only fruit brought in for eating. If they were brought in סתם, even he forbids the juice, and the next step challenges exactly this point.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
Olives from which he squeezed oil
and grapes from which he squeezed wine,
and he brought them in, whether for food or for liquids,
what seeps out of them is forbidden.
Mulberries from which he squeezed juice
and pomegranates from which he squeezed juice,
and he brought them in for food:
what seeps out of them is permitted;
for liquids, or without specifying:

phrases.aramaic: הַיּוֹצֵא מֵהֶן אָסוּר, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: what seeps out of them is forbidden. These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
And the Sages say:
whether for food or for liquids,
what seeps out of them is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support רב נחמן בר יצחק
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim that the dispute is about תותים and רמונים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording רבי יהודה and the חכמים on mulberries and pomegranates

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה really forbid fruit brought in with no stated purpose?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions how רבי יהודה could forbid the סתם case, citing a משנה where animal milk that comes out unwillingly does not count as a liquid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יהודה really hold that the unspecified case is forbidden? But we learned in a משנה: A woman's milk makes food able to become impure whether it came out willingly or unwillingly. An animal's milk does so only if it came out willingly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא's report that רבי יהודה forbids the סתם case. It quotes a משנה whose view seems to point the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that animal milk dripping out without the owner wanting it is not treated as a liquid. That suggests a liquid nobody intended does not count, which should make the סתם case permitted. The quoted משנה continues in the next steps, and the גמרא spells out how it connects to רבי יהודה's view on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes food able to receive טומאה (as a liquid)

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yehuda hold that the unspecified case is forbidden?!
But we learned in a mishnah:
A woman's milk makes food susceptible to impurity
whether it came out willingly or unwillingly.

phrases.aramaic: חֲלֵב בְּהֵמָה אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא אֶלָּא לְרָצוֹן.
phrases.english: An animal's milk makes food susceptible only if it came out willingly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges one detail of the ברייתא just quoted
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that רבי יהודה forbids the juice in the סתם case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה treats unintended animal milk as not a liquid, which implies that liquid without clear intent does not count. That conflicts with forbidding the סתם case.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's קל וחומר about animal milk
steps.stepSummary: Inside the quoted משנה, רבי עקיבא argues with a קל וחומר that animal milk should count as a liquid even when it comes out unwillingly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: It is a קל וחומר. A woman's milk is meant only for small children, yet it makes food susceptible whether it came out willingly or not. Animal milk is meant for both children and adults. Isn't it logical that it should make food susceptible whether it came out willingly or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the same משנה. Here רבי עקיבא challenges its ruling on animal milk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His logic is that animal milk is more important than a woman's milk because more people use it. So it should be treated as a liquid at least as strictly, even when it drips out on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: Argument from a lesser case to a greater case

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: קַל וָחוֹמֶר הוּא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said: It is an a fortiori argument:
Just as a woman's milk,
which is meant only for small children,
makes food susceptible whether willingly or unwillingly,
animal milk, which is meant
for both young and old,
is it not logical that it should make food susceptible
both willingly and unwillingly?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: קַל וָחוֹמֶר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quoted משנה with רבי עקיבא's objection to its ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that animal milk counts as a liquid only when it comes out willingly
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Animal milk is used more widely than a woman's milk, so it should be at least as strict.

steps.title: The חכמים reject the קל וחומר: a woman's blood is also a liquid
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer רבי עקיבא that a woman's milk is stricter because even the blood from her wound counts as a liquid. Their answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: A woman's milk makes food susceptible even when it comes out unwillingly, because the blood of her wound also makes food susceptible. Does that mean animal milk should make food susceptible... (continued)
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים begin to break רבי עקיבא's קל וחומר. Their answer runs into the next passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They show that a woman's milk has a special strictness: a liquid from her body, even blood from a wound, counts. That gives her milk a stricter starting point, so animal milk cannot simply be compared to it.
steps.confusionAlert: This back-and-forth between רבי עקיבא and the חכמים is still part of the quoted משנה. It is not yet the גמרא's own answer to the challenge against רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אִם טָמֵא חֲלֵב הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁלֹּא לְרָצוֹן,
phrases.english: If a woman's milk makes food susceptible even when unwilling,
that is because the blood of her wound makes food susceptible,
shall the milk of an animal make food susceptible...
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A woman's milk has an extra strictness (even her wound blood counts as a liquid) that animal milk lacks
